questions.prompt: A gym owner says, “Half our texts are people trying to freeze or cancel. Can the AI deal with those?” What’s the most accurate answer?

options.text: Yes, it freezes memberships and cancels following your own policy
It can reply to those texts, but staff still make every change
Only if the client sends the request through the web chat box
Yes, and it waives any late-cancel fee so the client stays happy

questions.reveal: The agent takes actions in the account, and cancellations follow the cancellation policy the studio set up.

questions.prompt: Which channels does the support agent answer from the inbox?

options.text: Text and email only, with web chat going straight to staff
Text, email and web chat, all in the one shared inbox
Web chat on the studio's website, and nothing else
Email only, while texts are handled by the sequences

questions.reveal: Text, email and web chat all land in the all-in-one inbox, and the agent can answer each of them.

questions.prompt: An owner wants to personally call anyone asking about her premium membership. What do you show her?

options.text: A sequence that emails her each time that membership is viewed
Turning off the sales agent so nobody discusses memberships
Setting that question to escalate to her instead of the agent
A report of who bought the premium membership in the last month

questions.reveal: Owners choose what goes to a person. Escalated conversations land in the inbox and staff get notified.

questions.prompt: An owner wants the AI to book classes but never touch payments or refunds. Can she do that?

options.text: No. Payments and refunds come bundled with booking requests
Only by turning the AI off at night when the payments run
Only if a staff member approves every message it sends
Yes. Each request type is its own switch she controls

questions.reveal: Each request type can be switched on or off, so she turns on booking and leaves payments and refunds off.

questions.prompt: Which of these can an owner set in the agent's customization?

options.text: Brand voice, response length and style, and example messages
The exact script for every question it's allowed to answer
Which clients see the agent, sorted by their last visit date
The hours of the day when the agent is allowed to reply

questions.reveal: Owners set the name, brand voice, response length (concise, standard or detailed), response style and example messages.

questions.prompt: An owner turned the agent on, and its setup score says “average.” What should she do first?

options.text: Switch off every request type until the score reaches high
Add the missing details it flags, like membership descriptions
Set the response length to detailed so it says more each time
Wait a few weeks for the agent to learn from her staff's replies

questions.reveal: The setup score reads the account and lists what's missing. Filling those gaps moves it toward a high setup.

questions.prompt: A boutique owner says, “Our brand is warm and a bit cheeky. Will the AI sound like a robot?” What do you show?

options.text: The example clients who have already chatted with the agent
The escalation settings so staff can answer the fun questions
The brand voice setting, with options like friendly or playful
A sequence template she can copy for her welcome messages

questions.reveal: Brand voice is a setting. She can pick a tone and add example messages so replies sound like her studio.

questions.prompt: An owner worries she has no time to teach an AI everything. What’s true about setup?

options.text: It learns everything on its own once it's switched on
You'll need to write an answer for each possible question
Your front desk trains it by chatting with it each week
Onboarding sets it up with you; the score shows what's missing

questions.reveal: Onboarding walks through the setup with the owner, and the setup score points to exactly what to add.

questions.prompt: What does the sales agent's follow-up tone setting control?

options.text: How pushy follow-ups are, from gentle reminder to high urgency
Which leads it contacts first, based on how recently they joined
Whether follow-ups go out by text, by email or by both channels
How many times it follows up before it hands a lead to staff

questions.reveal: The tone options are gentle reminder, encouraging push and high urgency.

questions.prompt: A studio wants the AI to convert more leads. Which sequence message sets it up best?

options.text: “Our intro offer ends Friday. Book now at the link below.”
“Welcome! Here's our schedule and our full price list.”
“What made you curious about reformer? Any questions?”
“We'd love to see you. Follow us on Instagram for news.”

questions.reveal: A message that ends in a question invites a reply, and a reply opens the conversation the agent picks up.

questions.prompt: Where does the sales agent pick up a lead's reply to a sequence?

options.text: In a separate sales app the owner checks once a day
In the shared inbox, where the conversation opens
On the website chat box, the next time the lead visits
In a weekly email report sent to the studio's owner

questions.reveal: Replies land in the inbox as a conversation, and the agent takes it from there.

questions.prompt: What does the sales agent screen track for the studio?

options.text: The leads it has contacted and the revenue it has generated
Each lead's ad source and the cost of every lead it captured
The setup score for each sequence the studio has switched on
Which staff member closed each sale the agent handed over

questions.reveal: Leads contacted and revenue are on the screen. On a demo, point to the owner's own results once she's live, not another studio's numbers.

questions.prompt: A day spa owner says she'll switch only if she gets an AI chatbot tied to booking. What do you ask first?

options.text: Which AI tools she has already tried, and why they didn't work
Whether she'd sign today if you show her the chatbot right now
Whether her staff would be comfortable with an AI on the inbox
What she wants it to handle, and what she pays for that now

questions.reveal: The job decides what you demo. Her spend across every tool doing that job gives you the comparison.

questions.prompt: A prospect loves her current software's AI because it writes her monthly KPI reports. What's the right move?

options.text: Show the agent anyway, since it does more than reporting AI does
Be clear our agent is customer-facing, then find what else matters
Tell her our reports library makes an AI report unnecessary
Say reporting AI is coming soon so it doesn't block the deal

questions.reveal: Momence's AI handles customer conversations. Say so plainly, and don't promise a roadmap item.

questions.prompt: A prospect says, “My current software has an AI chat on the website too.” What's the best response?

options.text: “That's not really AI, it's just an FAQ dressed up as a chat.”
“Theirs only answers questions. Ours is the only one that books.”
“What does it handle for you today, and where does it fall short?”
“Most of those tools are a few years behind what we've built.”

questions.reveal: Acknowledge it and ask. Don't make claims about a competitor's AI that you can't verify.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the agent is safe to make on a demo?

options.text: It never gets an answer wrong, so staff needn't check it
It pays for itself within the first month for most studios
It runs your reports and tells you your churn each month
It escalates what it can't handle to a staff member

questions.reveal: Escalation to staff was shown in several demos. Payback claims and "never wrong" are promises you can't back up.

questions.prompt: After seeing the AI, a prospect says, “Who can even afford all this?” What's the strongest response?

options.text: Start with sequences, and add the AI once those bring replies
Show her another studio's revenue from the agent last month
Offer the agent free for a few months so the price stops mattering
Drop the marketing suite so the agent fits inside her budget

questions.reveal: Sequences first is the cheaper start and the base the agent works on. Don't concede before you know the core need.

questions.prompt: Mid-demo, a prospect asks what the AI costs, and you're not sure. What do you do?

options.text: Give a rough figure so the conversation keeps its momentum
Quote from the pricing calculator or confirm with your manager
Say it's included in the top plan so she doesn't worry about it
Tell her the price changes too often to give her a number

questions.reveal: AI pricing is still being confirmed. A guessed number becomes the number she remembers.

questions.prompt: Why does starting with sequences set the AI up to work better later?

options.text: Sequences train the agent's brand voice before it's switched on
The agent can only reply to clients who were in a sequence
Replies to sequences ending in a question hand leads to the agent
Sequences raise the setup score from average up to high

questions.reveal: The agent works conversations. Sequences that end in a question create the replies it picks up.

questions.prompt: A prospect asks if clients will be told they're talking to an AI. You're not certain. What do you say?

options.text: “Yes, it always says it's an AI, so you don't need to worry.”
“No, clients can't tell the difference, which is the beauty of it.”
“It depends on the client's settings in the Momence app.”
“Good question. I'll confirm exactly how that works and follow up.”

questions.reveal: When you're not sure, say so and follow up with the confirmed answer. Don't hedge your way into a guess.
